why: The student thinks StdDraw.point(256, 256) lands in the middle of the default window, which is the PixelCoordinates misconception: the default scale is the unit square, so the point is outside the canvas and does not show, and the window holds only the square centred at (0.5, 0.5).

concepts.quote: The square uses 0.5 as the centre
concepts.why: It correctly says the square is centred on (x, y) but says nothing about its size (side 2r = 0.5) or its corners.

concepts.quote: the point uses pixels, so both are in the middle
concepts.why: It matches PixelCoordinates: StdDraw uses unit-square coordinates by default, so (256, 256) is off the canvas and does not appear.
No setXscale or setYscale call is made, so the default unit-square scale applies and pixel values are not a coordinate system.
The code and the answer do not involve Math.round.
